claim.pdf_says:
11.3.2  General format

  CLASS-ID.  object-class-name-1 [ AS literal-1 ]  [ IS  FINAL ]
      [ INHERITS FROM { object-class-name-2 }  ... ]
      [ USING { parameter-name-1 }  ... ] .

-- underlining on CLASS-ID, AS, FINAL, INHERITS, USING; IS and FROM printed WITHOUT underlining.
claim.markdown_says:

-- fenced, textually exact, but with no record of which words are underlined and therefore required.
claim.why_it_matters: This is the normative general format for the CLASS-ID paragraph. Losing the underlining erases the required/optional distinction: the standard permits 'CLASS-ID. C-1 FINAL.' (IS is an optional word) and 'INHERITS { C-2 }' (FROM is an optional word). A reader of the markdown alone would implement both as mandatory and reject legal source.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED by independent glyph inspection, and the strongest available refutation (that dropping underlining is a global transcription policy) is disproved by the transcription's own adjacent pages.

1) PDF glyph evidence (E:/Temp/specrecon/v294/spec_p294.png, 300 dpi, plus 2x/3x crops fmt_zoom.png, z_line1_tail.png, z_line2.png). A horizontal-run scan of the general-format block (rows scanned for dark runs >= 25 px) finds underline rules on exactly six rows and three x-spans:
   y=936-937: x 297-467 (CLASS-ID, 171 px), x 929-968 (AS, 40 px), x 1274-1384 (FINAL, 111 px)
   y=1009-1010: x 384-566 (INHERITS, 183 px)
   y=1081-1082: x 384-497 (USING, 114 px)
   'IS' occupies x ~1211-1245 on line 1, falling in the gap between the AS rule (ends 968) and the FINAL rule (starts 1274) -- no rule beneath it. 'FROM' occupies x ~598-713 on line 2, beyond the end of the INHERITS rule (566) -- no rule beneath it. The 25 px detection threshold is well below the 40 px 'AS' rule that WAS detected, so a rule under the ~34 px 'IS' or the ~115 px 'FROM' would have been found had one existed. The 3x crops confirm this visually: '] [ IS  FINAL ]' shows a clean rule under FINAL only, and '[ INHERITS FROM {' shows a clean rule under INHERITS only. The claim's description of the printed underlining is exactly correct, word for word.

2) The markdown loses it. specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 12813-12819 carry a bare ``` fence with no <u> markup and no following figure-notes block. Verified in the master file, not merely the extracted work unit.

3) Not a formatting/reflow/furniture difference, and not a global convention. The transcription has TWO established, live mechanisms for preserving underlining, both in use in this very chapter on the immediately surrounding pages:
   - inline <u> tags (97 occurrences file-wide), e.g. line 12885 (§11.4.2 FACTORY, p296): '<u>FACTORY</u>. [ <u>IMPLEMENTS</u> { interface-name-1 } ... . ]'; and line 12933 (§11.5.2 FUNCTION-ID, p297): '<u>FUNCTION-ID</u>. function-prototype-name-1 [ <u>AS</u> literal-1 ] IS <u>PROTOTYPE</u>.' -- which renders the very same 'IS is not underlined' discriminator correctly.
   - '> **Figure notes (...)**' blocks (225 occurrences), e.g. line 13034 (§11.7.2 METHOD-ID, p299), which states explicitly: '`IS` in the `[ IS FINAL ]` bracket is *not* underlined.'
   §11.3.2 sits between these and uses neither. It is an outlier against the file's own convention, not the convention itself.

4) The consequence is normative and is stated correctly. Per the transcription's own §5.2.2 (line 2628) keywords 'are shown in uppercase and underlined in general formats [and] are required', and §5.2.3 (line 2641) optional words 'are shown in uppercase and not underlined [and] may be written to add clarity'. Therefore the un-underlined IS and FROM are optional words, and 'CLASS-ID. C-1 FINAL.' and 'INHERITS class-2' are legal source. A compiler built from the markdown alone would make both mandatory and reject conforming programs -- a real, spec-visible defect, not a cosmetic one.
verdict.corrected_description:
The finding is real and the claim's characterization of both sources is accurate; two refinements for the ledger.

(a) Scope -- this is NOT a systemic 'the transcription never records underlining' issue. specs/ISO_COBOL.md preserves underlining routinely, via inline <u> tags (§11.4.2 FACTORY line 12885, §11.5.2 FUNCTION-ID lines 12929/12933) and via '> **Figure notes**' blocks (§11.7.2 METHOD-ID line 13034, which even spells out that IS in '[ IS FINAL ]' is not underlined). §11.3.2 CLASS-ID at lines 12813-12819 is a localized regression against that established convention, so the fix is to restore markup on this figure, not to invent a new policy.

(b) Sibling defect -- the identical loss occurs at §11.6.2 INTERFACE-ID (page 298, master lines ~12971-12975), also a bare fence: 'INTERFACE-ID.  interface-name-1  [ AS literal-1 ] / [ INHERITS FROM { interface-name-2 } … ] / [ USING { parameter-name-1 } … ] .' It carries the same INHERITS FROM / USING shape and therefore the same lost required/optional distinction. Per the project's sweep rule, both should be repaired in one change set.

(c) Minor imprecision in the claim, not affecting the verdict: the illustrative 'INHERITS { C-2 }' writes the metalanguage braces as if they were source characters; the braces are grouping symbols for the ellipsis, so the legal source is 'INHERITS class-2'. The claim's PDF quotation also normalizes some inter-token spacing.

Corrected markdown for §11.3.2 should read, in the file's own <u> style: '<u>CLASS-ID</u>.  object-class-name-1 [ <u>AS</u> literal-1 ] [ IS  <u>FINAL</u> ] / [ <u>INHERITS</u> FROM { object-class-name-2 } … ] / [ <u>USING</u> { parameter-name-1 } … ] .'
